selectedOriginals.caption: Five-segment panorama of Hoboken Terminal with Jersey City skyline in the background, as viewed from Pier A Park, Hoboken, New Jersey.
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full2015 panorama inspected individually: six open elliptical river arches with bronze/brown structural facing and green trim, open ferry slips/finger-pier piles, plain pale north end wall with two rows of small windows, tall brown reconstructed four-face clock tower, small green roof cupola and large raised Lackawanna letters. Water, boats and neighboring skyline separate.

selectedOriginals.caption: Exterior of Hoboken Terminal. Hoboken, New Jersey, USA.
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full2010 original inspected individually: limestone ground floor with deep double entry and overhanging canopy, three tall multi-pane bronze/brown windows, ornamented green copper pilasters, garland/roundel upper surrounds, dentils, date1907 curved pediment, and brown clock tower behind. Signs are visible but lettering/geometry must be authored, not photographic pixels.

additionalInspected.caption: Hoboken Terminal
additionalInspected.inspection: 2012 full4592x3056 original individually inspected: six true open river arches with elliptical undersides, brown/bronze corrugated structural surrounds/green edge and diamond panels, deep open bays with internal steel columns and metal grilles, five modern white curved gangway canopies, roof parapet rail, raised Lackawanna sign, small green cupola and brown reconstructed clock tower. Boats not included.

sources.inspection: Primary1973/2004 nomination relevant descriptions and rendered plans54/57/58 inspected. Six elliptical river openings, five gabled plaza pavilions, canopy and own rail waiting-room/low south rooms are distinct from western Train Shed, Baggage/YMCA and Pullman buildings. River frontage566ft2.125in(~172.57m) includes south restaurant; main waiting room100x90ft. Site plans show rear concourse/river-side pier rooms with open slips, not a solid full-depth block. Original225ft tower preceded current replica; current project manager225ft used for reconstruction.

Operator2008 restored tower dedication record read: new replica of original, four12ft clock faces, four-foot copper Lackawanna letters and hip/cupola roof. Old tower height cited230ft conflicts operator2006 historical203ft; do not silently treat either as surveyed restored height.
Operator2006 radio-tower removal/reconstruction record read; historical tower203ft conflicts2008 statement230ft. Restoration era is relevant; pre2007 originals cannot establish reconstructed tower.

Actual reconstruction project manager/designer record read: restored tower225ft(68.58m), distinct from entire54-acre yard. Prefer project-as-built dimensional control provisionally, reconcile actual measured footprint/photographic proportions.

Operator2025 record read: first/second floor ferry building undergoing restoration. Model era will follow selected2010/2015 originals; current construction is not assumed finished from future-use prose.

Plain north ferry wall and waterfront finger piers belong to era-specific scope; surrounding boats/docks/large platform roofs must not be accidentally included.

scope: Copper ferry/rail terminal, six open elliptical river arches, five gabled plaza bays, waiting-room facade, replica clock tower, skylights, pier supports and five gangways.
limitations: Surviving exterior follows selected2010/2015 originals and focused2011/2012 photographs; official2004 site/floor plans and independent mapped outlines separate own ferry/rail terminal from western platform train sheds, baggage/YMCA and Pullman buildings. Fine ornaments, exact elevations, below-water piles and hidden openings remain authored estimates.

Reconstructed tower225ft(68.58m) follows actual project manager STV and historic nomination; operator historical203/230ft statements conflict and are recorded. Four12ft clock faces follow operator reconstruction record. Brown replica tower and green/bronze copper facades are retained. No radio tower or future redevelopment reconstructed.

Six open ferry facade arches, own concrete/steel pier supports, five modern white gangway canopies and own waiting-room/south rooms retained. Boats, detached pontoons/dock furniture, streets/plaza, western platform/train sheds and neighboring baggage/Pullman buildings excluded. Gangways are fixed representative poses; tide/water/pile embedment is approximate. No source photo/plan pixels redistributed.
Independent terrain remains unchanged. Mixed marine/land site needs explicit contact review; no seabed or tidal survey is available. Footprint replacement disabled.
